description: Issue #948-F8: neutralizes ConfiguredAllowlistDashboardEgressPolicy.IsAllowedAsync's Methods gate by forcing the check to never actually run via a compile-preserving `false &&` prefix (same established pattern as the sibling write/send-time mutants). This reintroduces the exact defect the Methods field's own consumer requirement closes: an entry configured with Methods = ["GET"] (intended to let a REST widget only GET a specific internal host, not POST/DELETE/etc. to it) instead approves ANY method to that host/IP/port -- i.e. DashboardEgressAllowlistEntry.Methods becomes exactly the 'destination field with no in-repo consumer' issue #948-F8 explicitly required NOT to ship. red_test is the non-matching-method denial; green_test is the matching-method approval, proving the mutant's blast radius is specifically the Methods gate, not host/port matching (which stays correct either way).

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Dashboard.Conf: Assert\.IsFalse failed\. an entry restricted to GET must not approve a POST destination

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured by applying the patch manually and running exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) before writing this file, then reverting the manual patch application and letting run_mutant.py apply/run/revert it itself for the actual gate run. The declared red test failed with exactly this message (MSTest's own Assert.IsFalse -- confirmed identical between Debug and Release). Also ran the full ConfiguredAllowlistDashboardEgressPolicyTests filter (23 tests, including the new TenantId gating group and all pre-existing Host/Port matching tests) under the same mutant beforehand: only the one declared test failed; IsAllowedAsync_MatchingMethod_Allows and IsAllowedAsync_MethodMatchIsCaseInsensitive and IsAllowedAsync_NullMethods_AllowsAnyMethod all stayed green (expected -- disabling the check only removes a REJECTION path, so anything that was already supposed to be approved stays approved), and every TenantId/Host/Port test (an independent code block, untouched by this patch) stayed green.
